result.oneSentenceSummary: Count detection misses aliased and whitespace variants of count()
result.improvedCode:
def transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(
    query_columns: Sequence[str],
) -> list[str]:
    """
    Transform aggregation functions to use sum(sample_weight) instead of count()
    for error upsampling. Only called when all projects are allowlisted.
    """
    import re

    count_pattern = re.compile(r"^count\s*\(\s*\)\s*(?:as\s+(\w+))?$", re.IGNORECASE)
    transformed_columns = []
    for column in query_columns:
        match = count_pattern.match(column.strip())

        if match:
            # Any canonical form or alias of count() becomes sum of sample weights
            alias = match.group(1) or "count"
            transformed_columns.append(f"upsampled_count() as {alias}")

        else:
            transformed_columns.append(column)

    return transformed_columns

judge.titleReason: The title accurately names the defect: count detection fails to recognize aliased forms and forms with whitespace inside the parentheses.
judge.fixReason: The case-insensitive regex on the stripped column matches zero-argument count with inner whitespace and an optional alias, preserves the alias case, defaults the alias to count, and leaves other columns unchanged and in order.
